channel.title: NBC Sports Fantasy Football News
channel.description: Latest player news and analysis for fantasy football from NBC Sports.

item.title: Jordan Schultz reports the Saints plan to release S Justin Reid at his request.
item.description: Reid’s having his worst season in the league per PFF’s charting data, having compiled a 49.1 PFF defensive grade and his second-worst coverage grade as a pro at 47.8. That said, Reid has plenty of versatility and wants to seek work with a contender. It sounds like he’ll likely find a new home in the near future.-Rivers McCown

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports that Puka Nacua will serve a three-game suspension for violating the league’s personal conduct policy while on injured reserve.
item.description: Schefter notes that the timing of Nacua’s suspension “could potentially save him a substantial amount of money.” Suspended players are not paid, and Nacua is in the final year of his rookie contract. Serving the suspension now “will cost him a lot less than serving it on his next contract, which is expected to be far more lucrative.” Schefter does not say whether he thinks the Rams will be the team that pays him, but a big payday is apparently still expected. Players are required to miss four games on injured reserve. Nacua has already missed one game. The Rams are on bye this week. He will spend the remainder of his injured reserve stint while also serving his suspension, and he will be eligible to return for Week 15 against the Cowboys.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Kyler Gordon (shoulder) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description: Gordon, the Bears’ starting slot cornerback, is on the wrong side of questionable for this week’s game against the Saints. Bears DT Jeffery Simmons was limited by a knee injury, but DC Dennis Allen said he does not expect the injury to impact Simmons’ availability.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter believes that the Titans or Chargers would host “an auction” for the 2027 NFL Draft’s No. 1 overall pick if either team gets it.
item.description: The Titans are currently in position to receive the No. 1 overall pick, and the Chargers are right behind them. Schefter spent much of the segment discussing the Titans, who Schefter says have “enough conviction” in Cam Ward that they would pass on the opportunity to draft Oklahoma State QB Drew Mestemaker. He cites the Dolphins, Jets, Cardinals and Browns as potential suitors. Poor play from Ward could still change minds in the Titans’ front office, but for now, it seems as though his job is secure.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Tommy Tremble (knee) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
item.description: Tremble, who had 48 yards last week against the Saints, is probably the preferred TE2 play between himself and Darren Waller if both players make it to Sunday’s game against the Ravens healthy. Each of them logged a limited session on Thursday after missing Wednesday.-Rivers McCown

item.title: Darren Waller (knee) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
item.description: He didn’t practice Wednesday, so this is a good sign for his availability. With Tommy Tremble also practicing though, we may remain in the Panthers TE Stasis where both players are taking too much volume off the table for you to want to start either of them in fantasy leagues.-Rivers McCown

item.title: Brock Bowers (ankle) resumed practicing on Thursday.
item.description: This is great to see. We expect Bowers to be listed as a limited participant, but his return to practice with an extra day to spare gives him a real chance to suit up in Week 11 against a Broncos defense that routinely surrenders catches and yardage to the tight end position. Bowers is an elite TE1 if active.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: ESPN’s Stephen Holder reports that the Colts have a “package of plays in the playbook” for Anthony Richardson, but it is unclear whether they will “ever” use them.
item.description: Holder stops short of making any declarative statements, but today’s article implies that some in the Colts’ organization may be wondering why their 24-year-old quarterback hasn’t at least been used as a situational player. Holder compares Daniel Jones’ poor play to positive remarks made by Colts defenders regarding Richardson’s explosive dual-threat abilities. Holder does note that the Colts have at least considered using Richardson’s “electric running ability” to give them “a spark,” but for whatever reason, that hasn’t happened yet. Richardson could be worth stashing in superflex leagues, though there is no guarantee that he will take the field on game day.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker said he considered leaving the Cowboys after being stripped of play-calling duties.
item.description: Parker was demoted after the Cowboys got rocked by the 49ers in Week 10. Defensive assistant Mike Pettine will call plays on defense for now. When asked about his future in Dallas, Parker could only say he will cross that bridge when he gets there. It sounds like he and the Cowboys will part ways after the season. Parker was a defensive backs coach in Denver and Philadelphia for five seasons before landing the Dallas defensive coordinator gig.-Kyle Dvorchak

item.title: Broncos signed CB Riley Moss to a four-year, $67 million contract extension.
item.description: The former third-round pick played almost exclusively on special teams as a rookie. He took over a starting role in his second season and never looked back. Moss has eight pass breakups and one interception this year. He led the league in PBUs in 2025. Moss was set to hit free agency next offseason. Instead, the Broncos got out ahead of him hitting the open market and kept him in town on a relatively affordable deal. Moss is just outside the 20 highest-paid corners on a per-year basis.-Kyle Dvorchak
